title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: the peace talks are over, and Krishna invites Karna up into his chariot for a ride outside the city.
carry: her milk fed him, her love kept him alive

segments.voice: Yesterday Krishna made the whole case for peace before the Kuru court, and Duryodhana refused. Your line: no one could say it was never offered.

A chariot rolls out through the gates of Hastinapura. The embassy has failed. Duryodhana won't give the Pandavas their share, and war is coming. But before Krishna goes, he does something odd. He calls Karna, Duryodhana's friend and champion, up beside him, and the two ride out of the city together, away from the crowd. What Krishna says on that ride could stop the war before it starts, and it rests on a secret about who Karna's mother is.
screen: `THE EMBASSY HAS FAILED.` → `KRISHNA CALLS KARNA UP` → `A SECRET ON THE ROAD`

segments.voice: Here is the secret. Karna is Kunti's son, born to her before she married Pandu. That makes him, Krishna says, the eldest brother of the five Pandavas. Then comes the offer. Come with me. Your brothers will touch your feet. You will be king, and Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne. Everything Karna has been denied, the rank, the family, the respect, is laid at his feet in one ride. Karna's answer is the heart of today. He says he already knows. Then he says why it changes nothing. His mother set him adrift as a newborn. A charioteer named Adhiratha found him, and Adhiratha's wife Radha raised him. Her milk fed him and her love kept him alive, he says, and he will not stop being her son for a crown. He married among the charioteer's people, and he has children there. And for years Duryodhana has stood by him when no one else would. He gave Duryodhana his word, and he means to keep it. Then he asks Krishna for one thing: don't tell Yudhishthira. If Yudhishthira learned that Karna was his elder brother, he would hand him the kingdom, and Karna would hand it straight to Duryodhana. Better that it stays secret. So a man is offered everything he ever wanted, and turns it down for the people who loved him first. Some readers hear loyalty in that. Some hear tragedy. The epic lets you hear both.
screen: `KARNA IS KUNTI'S FIRST SON` · `THE OFFER: BROTHERS AND A THRONE` · `RADHA RAISED ME; I STAY HER SON` · then, large: `DON'T TELL YUDHISHTHIRA`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one offer, large or small, that would cost you a bond with someone: a job, a move, a new circle. Breathing in, hold the offer; breathing out, hold the bond, and just notice where your attention settles, the way Karna weighed a throne against Radha. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer.
Udyoga. The preparing, the getting ready for war: the book where every side makes its choices before the fighting begins. Today, Karna made his.
Your line: her milk fed him, her love kept him alive. A crown on one side, a mother on the other, and the mother won. Day eight hundred seventeen, done.

original.note: the name of the Mahabharata's fifth book, the Udyoga Parva, the book of getting ready for war.

chat.says: Why would Karna turn down a throne and his real brothers?
options: Radha raised him and Duryodhana stood by him. He wouldn't break those bonds.
Krishna's offer came with no crown, only a place in the Pandava army.
He wanted the throne, but Kunti had already asked him to refuse it.
chat.meaning: Karna already knew he was Kunti's son. But Radha raised him and Duryodhana stood by him, and he would not break those bonds for a crown.

Karna.meaning: Kunti's first son, raised by a charioteer's family

Kunti.meaning: mother of the Pandavas, and secretly of Karna

Radha.meaning: the charioteer's wife who raised Karna as her own son

Adhiratha.meaning: the charioteer who found the newborn Karna adrift

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Krishna takes Karna in his chariot after the failed embassy; says that by law Kunti's son born before marriage counts as Pandu's son and the eldest; offers kingship with Yudhishthira serving him; Karna says he knows, names Adhiratha and Radha, his marriages and children among the sutas, his bond with Duryodhana, and asks that Yudhishthira not be told.
Krishna's offer is simplified ('Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne'); Ganguli's text has a longer list, including Draupadi; the script leaves that out deliberately.
The review assumes day 816 covered Krishna's embassy at the Kuru court; adjust if that day's script ends elsewhere.
Trapdoor floor 3 is framed as 'some readers'; a Keeper may prefer a different scholarly note.
